chunks: By this chain of transmission, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Sa'd ibn Aws, from Bilal ibn Yahya al-Absi.

He said: When Ammar (may God be pleased with him) was killed, they came to Hudhayfa, and they said: O Abu Abdullah! This man has been killed, and the people have differed, so what do you say? He said: Well then, since you insist, seat me up. He said: So they propped him against the chest of a man from among them, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) saying: Abu al-Yaqthan is upon the natural disposition (fitra) — three times — he will never leave it until he dies.

key_terms.أَبُو الْيَقْظَانِ: Abu al-Yaqthan (the Wakeful), the kunya of Ammar ibn Yasir
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: fitra, the innate natural disposition toward truth and righteousness

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ammar ibn Yasir and the fitra?
ai.summary: This hadith records Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman's testimony about Ammar ibn Yasir after his killing at the Battle of Siffin (37 AH). When people came to the ailing Hudhayfa seeking guidance about the division among Muslims, he invoked the Prophet's triple declaration that Abu al-Yaqthan (Ammar's kunya) was upon the fitra — the innate, pure disposition toward truth. This served as an implicit condemnation of those who fought against Ammar, as the Prophet had certified that Ammar would remain on the right path until his death.
